prompt: Which orbitals combine to form sp hybrid orbitals?

choices.text: The 2s orbital and a single 2p orbital

choices.why: That combination gives sp2 hybrids.
That combination gives sp3 hybrids.
A hybrid includes the s orbital; sp means one s and one p.

explanation: To account for a triple bond, carbon's 2s orbital hybridizes with only a single p orbital. Two sp hybrid orbitals result, and two p orbitals remain unchanged.

prompt: How many sp hybrid orbitals does an sp-hybridized carbon have?
explanation: Combining the 2s orbital with one 2p orbital gives two sp hybrid orbitals.

prompt: How many unhybridized p orbitals remain on an sp-hybridized carbon?
explanation: Only one of the three 2p orbitals is used to make the two sp hybrids, so two p orbitals remain unchanged. They form the two π bonds of a triple bond.

prompt: What is the angle between the two sp hybrid orbitals on a carbon, in degrees?
explanation: The two sp orbitals are oriented 180° apart on the x axis, with the two remaining p orbitals perpendicular to them on the y and z axes.

prompt: What bonds make up the carbon–carbon triple bond in acetylene?

choices.text: One sp–sp σ bond and two p–p π bonds

choices.why: Only one σ bond can form head-on between two carbons; the other two bonds come from sideways p overlap.

choices.text: Two σ bonds and one π bond
choices.why: A triple bond has one σ bond and two π bonds.
The first bond between two atoms is always a σ bond, here from sp–sp overlap.

explanation: The sp hybrids on the two carbons overlap head-on to form an sp–sp σ bond, while the p_z orbitals form a p_z–p_z π bond and the p_y orbitals a p_y–p_y π bond. Six electrons are shared in all.

prompt: How many electrons are shared in a carbon–carbon triple bond?
explanation: A triple bond is one σ bond and two π bonds, each with two electrons: 3 × 2 = 6 electrons shared.

prompt: What is the shape of an acetylene molecule, H–C≡C–H?

choices.text: Linear, with H–C–C bond angles of 180°

choices.why: That is ethylene, whose carbons are sp2.
That is the geometry around sp3 carbons, as in methane.
The sp orbitals point 180° apart, so the molecule is straight.

explanation: As suggested by sp hybridization, acetylene is a linear molecule with H–C–C bond angles of 180°.

prompt: What is the C≡C bond length in acetylene, in picometers?
explanation: The C≡C bond in acetylene is 120 pm long, shorter than the C=C bond (134 pm) and the C–C bond (153 pm).

prompt: What is the strength of the C≡C bond in acetylene, in kJ/mol?
explanation: The C≡C bond is about 965 kJ/mol (231 kcal/mol), the strongest of any carbon–carbon bond.

prompt: What is the length of a C–H bond in acetylene, in picometers?
explanation: The C–H bonds in acetylene are 106 pm long and have a strength of 558 kJ/mol (133 kcal/mol).

prompt: Which list puts the carbon–carbon bonds in order from shortest to longest?

choices.why: That is longest to shortest. More shared electrons pull the carbons closer, so the triple bond is shortest.
The triple bond (120 pm) is shorter than the double bond (134 pm).

choices.text: All three are the same length
choices.why: They differ: 120 pm for C≡C, 134 pm for C=C, and 153 pm for C–C.

explanation: From Table 1.9.1: acetylene's C≡C is 120 pm, ethylene's C=C 134 pm, and ethane's C–C 153 pm. The triple bond is the shortest and strongest carbon–carbon bond.

prompt: Which of these molecules has the strongest C–H bonds?

choices.why: Methane's C–H bonds (439 kJ/mol) are weaker than those of ethylene and acetylene.
Ethane's C–H bonds (421 kJ/mol) are the weakest of the four in Table 1.9.1.
Ethylene's (464 kJ/mol) are stronger than those of the sp3 carbons, but acetylene's (558 kJ/mol) are stronger still.

explanation: Table 1.9.1 gives C–H bond strengths of 421 kJ/mol (ethane), 439 (methane), 464 (ethylene) and 558 (acetylene). The sp carbon's C–H bonds are the strongest, and also the shortest (106 pm).

prompt: In propyne, CH3C≡CH, how are the carbons hybridized?

choices.text: The CH3 carbon is sp3, and the two triple-bond carbons are sp

choices.why: The CH3 carbon has only single bonds, so it is sp3.

choices.text: The CH3 carbon is sp3, and the triple-bond carbons are sp2
choices.why: Carbons in a triple bond are sp; sp2 goes with double bonds.
The two triple-bond carbons are sp.

explanation: In propyne, the CH3 carbon is sp3 and the triple-bond carbons are sp. The C≡C–C and H–C≡C bond angles are about 180°.

prompt: What value would you predict for the H–C≡C bond angle in propyne, CH3C≡CH, in degrees?
explanation: The triple-bond carbons are sp-hybridized, with their two sp orbitals 180° apart, so the H–C≡C and C≡C–C angles are about 180°.

prompt: How are the two π bonds of acetylene's triple bond arranged?

choices.text: One forms from the p_y orbitals and one from the p_z orbitals, at right angles to each other
Both form from the p_z orbitals
choices.why: Each carbon has one p_y and one p_z orbital; the two π bonds use different pairs.

choices.text: They lie along the line between the nuclei
choices.why: That is where the σ bond's electrons are. π bonds lie off the axis.

choices.text: One forms from sp orbitals and one from p orbitals
choices.why: The sp orbitals form σ bonds; both π bonds come from p orbitals.

explanation: The p_z orbitals from each carbon form a p_z–p_z π bond by sideways overlap, and the p_y orbitals overlap similarly to form a p_y–p_y π bond. The two p orbitals on each carbon are perpendicular, so the two π bonds are too.
